abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel paradigm for ontological knowledge representation that fundamentally reconceptualizes how semantic structures capture dynamic real-world phenomena. Traditional ontology models suffer from static representational frameworks that inadequately address knowledge evolution in complex domains. We propose the Emergent Semantic Hierarchy (ESH) framework, which leverages computational creativity principles to enable ontologies that autonomously generate novel concept relationships through abductive reasoning mechanisms. Our theoretical contribution establishes formal foundations for self-modifying semantic structures, demonstrating that knowledge representations can exhibit emergent properties previously thought incompatible with formal ontological commitments. The framework introduces configurable semantic plasticity parameters that govern the rate and scope of concept evolution, supported by a comprehensive algebraic specification. We validate the theoretical soundness of ESH through rigorous proofs demonstrating consistency preservation during ontological transformation and establishing decidability bounds for reasoning over dynamically evolving knowledge bases. This paradigm shift enables knowledge management systems to maintain semantic coherence while adapting to novel information streams, fundamentally altering the relationship between ontological stability and knowledge acquisition. The research contributes a new theoretical lens for understanding how data semantics can be designed to exhibit organic growth characteristics, opening avenues for knowledge engineering approaches that transcend traditional rigid taxonomic structures.

Data quality assessment in integrated information systems remains insufficiently addressed by existing multi-dimensional frameworks that treat quality dimensions as independent constructs. This paper presents an enhanced theoretical model for data quality evaluation that explicitly accounts for inter-dimensional dependencies and contextual relevance weights. Our approach builds upon the信息系统 perspective of data as organizational assets while introducing a novel Dependency-Aware Quality Calculus (DAQC) that formalizes how dimensions such as accuracy, completeness, and timeliness mutually influence each other within specific operational contexts. We derive a set of theoretical propositions establishing the mathematical properties of quality score aggregation under dependency constraints, demonstrating that naive independent evaluation systematically underestimates overall data fitness for use. The model incorporates domain-specific weight adjustment mechanisms derived from knowledge management principles, enabling organizations to configure quality evaluation according to their particular information system requirements. Through systematic analysis of quality assessment scenarios across diverse data integration contexts, we establish conditions under which the proposed framework provides substantially improved predictive validity compared to traditional independent models. The theoretical contributions include formal characterizations of quality degradation propagation and conditions for quality paradoxes where apparent improvements in single dimensions may compromise holistic data value.

This paper presents NoSQLBench, a groundbreaking benchmark framework specifically engineered for evaluating NoSQL database systems under big data workloads. Existing database benchmarks inadequately capture the architectural diversity and operational characteristics of modern distributed data stores, producing misleading performance predictions. NoSQLBench introduces a fundamentally different evaluation methodology based on workload signature analysis and adaptive testing protocols that dynamically adjust to the specific characteristics of each database system under examination. The system architecture incorporates novel components including a Workload DNA Profiler that captures the essential operational patterns of target applications, a Topology-Aware Test Orchestrator that models realistic distribution scenarios, and an Interpretation Engine that provides contextually meaningful performance comparisons across heterogeneous systems. Our implementation supports comprehensive evaluation of graph data stores, document databases, key-value systems, and column-family architectures through a extensible plugin architecture. Extensive experimental validation across 12 representative NoSQL systems demonstrates that NoSQLBench produces performance insights that differ substantially from those generated by traditional benchmarks, revealing previously undocumented scaling behaviors and operational bottlenecks. The framework represents a paradigm shift in how database systems are evaluated, moving from standardized synthetic workloads toward intelligent, adaptive assessment methodologies.

This paper presents SemantIX, an improved data integration architecture that substantially advances automatic semantic mapping generation for heterogeneous data sources. Current approaches to schema matching and ontology alignment in data warehousing contexts suffer from limited recall when handling complex structural differences and inadequate exploitation of semantic knowledge encoded in existing taxonomies. SemantIX introduces a hybrid matching engine that synergistically combines deep learning-based similarity computation with constraint propagation techniques derived from conceptual modeling principles. The system architecture features a novel Iterative Refinement Pipeline that progressively improves mapping quality through successive validation cycles against data provenance information and user feedback. Key technical contributions include an attention-weighted feature extraction mechanism that prioritizes semantically significant schema elements and a conflict resolution module that handles contradictory mapping candidates through probabilistic reasoning. The implementation provides comprehensive support for both structured database systems and semi-structured data formats, with optimized processing pipelines for large-scale data integration scenarios. Extensive evaluation on standard benchmarks and a real-world healthcare data integration case demonstrates that SemantIX achieves mapping accuracy improvements of 23-41% compared to state-of-the-art systems while reducing computational overhead through intelligent caching strategies. The architecture is designed for practical deployment in knowledge-driven organizations requiring robust data governance capabilities.
